newsitem.title: GERMANY: SNB welcomes EMU plans for stability pact - Meyer.
newsitem.headline: SNB welcomes EMU plans for stability pact - Meyer.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) president Hans Meyer said the SNB welcomed plans to establish a stability pact among European Monetary Union members.

"I welcome the plans to secure, on the basis of a stability pact, that a stability-oriented finance policy will be carried out also after the start of Monetary Union," Meyer said in the text of a speech to be presented before the Swiss Economic Forum here later today.
Switzerland has elected not to participate in EMU.

His comments followed a meeting of EU finance ministers and central bank governors in Dublin over the weekend. The officials agreed, among other things, on a stability pact aimed at ensuring spending discipline among future EMU member governments.
Meyer said Switzerland would most stongly feel the impact of the developments surrounding EMU in the next few years. "This is true whether we are a member of EMU or not," he said.

"One way or the other, we have a major interest in seeing that the Monetary Union is a success, that is, that the future European Central Bank will pursue a stability-oriented monetary policy. The prerequisites for this are good," Meyer said.
If the goals are met and stability is achieved, this would also allow the SNB to continue to pursue its current policy.

"But if the introduction of a common currency leads to turbulences, then the Swiss franc would likely become more attractive. In such circumstances, carrying out our goal of a monetary policy in the general interest of our country would leave us walking a narrow path between securing proper liquidity and ensuring an orderly market development," he said.
"I wish for us, and for our European partners, that we will be spared this test," he added.
